mainTopic: When a נזיר's unassigned money (מעות סתומין) goes to נדבה, and what counts as assigned money (מפורשין)
overview: The amud opens at the end of a challenge. The rule that a dead person's unassigned money (מעות סתומין) goes to נדבה seemed special to a נזיר, yet a ברייתא applies it to people who owe bird-pairs (קינין). The גמרא answers that the משנה taught נזיר, and cases like קינין share the rule because they are similar. The limit is meant to exclude a different ברייתא. There, someone owes a חטאת for a sin and also vowed an unrelated עולה, and his unassigned money must be thrown into ים המלח. Next, רב אשי explains when money counts as assigned (מפורשין): even if the owner named the חטאת, עולה, and שלמים together in one sentence. A second version of רב אשי goes further: even saying 'for my obligation' is enough. Finally, רבא limits the נדבה rule. If the חטאת money has already been separated out, the remaining money counts as assigned.

steps.title: A ברייתא applies the rule of unassigned money to people who owe bird-pairs
steps.stepSummary: The end of a ברייתא about people who set aside money for their קינין: the money can be used for an animal חטאת or עולה, and if the owner dies, unassigned money goes to נדבה. This challenges the idea that the rule is only for a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: People who set aside money for their bird-pairs: if one wants to bring an animal חטאת with it, he may. If he wants an animal עולה, he may. If he died and had unassigned money, it goes to gift offerings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא that applies the 'unassigned money goes to נדבה' rule to people who owe קינין, not only to a נזיר. That is the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה taught this rule about a נזיר, which made it sound special to נזיר. This ברייתא shows the same rule for קינין, so how can it be a נזיר-only law? The exclamation 'יפלו לנדבה!' is the punch line of the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Bird-pairs: one bird brought as a חטאת and one as an עולה
Unassigned money: set aside for offerings without saying which coins are for which offering
Voluntary gift offerings, here meaning communal gift offerings
A sin-offering brought from an animal instead of a bird
A burnt-offering brought from an animal instead of a bird

steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the rule of מעות סתומין going to נדבה is unique to a נזיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא applies the same rule to people who owe קינין, so it cannot be limited to נזיר.

steps.title: The משנה taught נזיר, and bird-pairs are similar to it
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the משנה mentions נזיר, but קינין are similar, so they share the rule. The real purpose is to exclude a different case taught in another ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא taught נזיר, and those who owe bird-pairs, which are similar to it, work the same way. The point is to exclude what was taught in a ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that נזיר is not the only case. Cases like קינין that are similar also get the rule. It then sets up a ברייתא that shows which case is left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not 'only נזיר'. It is 'נזיר and cases like it'. The word ולאפוקי tells us the limit is meant to exclude a different kind of case, which the next step spells out.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of the משנה; here, 'he taught'
Which are similar to it
To exclude

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the קינין ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Widening the scope: the rule covers נזיר and similar cases, not only נזיר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule seemed to apply only to a נזיר, so the קינין ברייתא looked like a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: Similar cases like קינין share the rule. The limit is meant to exclude a different kind of case.

steps.title: The excluded case: an unrelated חטאת and עולה paid from 'my obligation' money
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: someone owes a חטאת, also vows an עולה, and sets aside money 'for my obligation'. He may not use it for either animal offering, and if he dies, the unassigned money goes to ים המלח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone owed a חטאת, said 'I take upon myself an עולה', set aside money, and said 'this is for my obligation'. If he wants to bring an animal חטאת with it, he may not. An animal עולה, he may not. If he died with unassigned money, it goes to ים המלח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that our rule excludes. Here the unassigned money does not go to נדבה; it is thrown away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חטאת comes from a sin, and the עולה comes from a separate vow, so they are not one package like a נזיר's offerings or a pair of birds. Since we cannot tell which coins belong to the חטאת, the money cannot go to gift offerings and must be destroyed. That is why the rule is 'נזיר and similar cases' only.

keyTerms.meaning: Obligated, owing an offering
'It is upon me': the wording of a vow to bring an offering
For my obligation
The Dead Sea, where forbidden money is thrown so no one benefits from it

steps.whatToRemember: Unassigned money goes to נדבה only for a נזיר and similar cases like קינין. When the offerings are unrelated obligations (a חטאת for a sin plus a vowed עולה), the money goes to ים המלח.

phrases.english: One who owed a sin-offering,

"This is for my obligation,"
phrases.notes: 'My obligation' could mean either the חטאת or the vowed עולה, so we do not know which one he meant.

phrases.aramaic: רָצָה לְהָבִיא בָּהֶן חַטַּאת בְּהֵמָה — לֹא יָבִיא.
phrases.english: if he wants to bring an animal sin-offering with it, he may not bring it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁהָיָה מְחוּיָּיב חַטָּאת, וְאָמַר: הֲרֵי עָלַי עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the case that step 2 said is excluded
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the offerings are unrelated obligations, unassigned money may not be used for either offering, and after death it goes to ים המלח.

steps.title: רב אשי: naming all three offerings together still counts as assigned
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that 'assigned money' (מפורשין) does not require dividing the coins offering by offering. Even saying 'these are for my חטאת, עולה, and שלמים' together counts as assigned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: When you said assigned money does not go to נדבה, do not think that means he said 'these for my חטאת, these for my עולה, and these for my שלמים'. Even if he said 'these are for my חטאת, my עולה, and my שלמים', they are assigned.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defines the term מפורשין from the משנה. Money counts as assigned even if the owner named all three offerings in one sentence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a נזיר, assigned money does not all go to נדבה; the חטאת part is treated differently. One might think 'assigned' requires naming separate piles of coins for each offering. רב אשי says that naming the offerings at all, even all together, takes the money out of the סתומין category.

keyTerms.meaning: Assigned money: designated for named offerings
Do not say, do not think
Peace-offerings
Even

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, money is מפורשין once the offerings are named, even all together in one sentence. Only money with no offerings named is סתומין.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'assigned' means each coin was given to a specific offering. Naming the three offerings together is enough.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
What you said, that assigned money does not,
phrases.notes: He means the משנה's rule that assigned money doesn't just go to gift offerings the way unassigned money does.

phrases.english: do not say it means he said:
"These are for my sin-offering, and these are for my burnt-offering,
and these are for my peace-offering."
Rather, even if he said:
"These are for my sin-offering and for my burnt-offering and for my peace-offering,"
it is assigned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הָא דְּאָמְרַתְּ מְפוֹרָשִׁין לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new point defining the משנה's term מפורשין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money is מפורשין even if the owner named the חטאת, עולה, and שלמים together without dividing the coins.

steps.title: A second version of רב אשי: even 'for my obligation' counts as assigned
steps.stepSummary: An איכא דאמרי version of רב אשי's statement: the money counts as assigned (מפורשין) even if the person only said 'these are for my obligation', without naming each offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רב אשי said it differently: Don't think the money counts as assigned only when he says 'These are for my חטאת, my עולה, and my שלמים.' Even if he just said 'These are for my obligation,' it counts as assigned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב אשי's statement from the step before. In this version, even a very general phrase makes the money count as assigned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the owner had to name all three offerings, even if he named them together in one sentence. In this version, he does not need to name any of them. Just saying 'for my obligation' (לחובתי) is enough to make the money count as מפורשין.

keyTerms.meaning: For my obligation: a general phrase that names no specific offering
Assigned money: money set aside for specific, named offerings
Don't say: introduces a ruling that is wider than you might have thought

steps.confusionAlert: In the ברייתא of step 3, the words 'for my obligation' did NOT make the money count as assigned. That was a different case: a person who owed a חטאת and had vowed an עולה. Here we are talking about a נזיר's own set of offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, wider version of רב אשי's definition of assigned money from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even the general statement 'these are for my obligation' makes a נזיר's money count as assigned (מפורשין).

steps.title: רבא: once the חטאת money is separated, the rest counts as assigned
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits the rule that unassigned money goes to נדבה. If the חטאת money has been separated out from the rest, the remaining money counts as assigned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The rule we taught, that unassigned money goes to gift offerings, applies only when everything is mixed together. If the money for the חטאת fell out and was separated from the rest, the remaining money is considered assigned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a limit to the rule that unassigned money (מעות סתומין) goes to נדבה. If the חטאת money is already separate, the rest is no longer treated as unassigned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unassigned money goes to נדבה because nobody knows which coins belong to which offering. Once the חטאת money is out of the mix, it is clear what the rest is for: the remaining offerings. So the remaining money is treated as מפורשין and is used for its proper offerings, not all of it as a gift עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Unassigned money: set aside for offerings without saying which coins are for which offering
Gift offerings, brought as a voluntary donation
The money meant for the sin-offering
That which we said: brings back an earlier rule so it can be limited or explained

steps.whatToRemember: Money for a נזיר's offerings counts as assigned if he names the offerings (even all together), and in one version even if he only says 'for my obligation'. According to רבא, once the חטאת money is separated out, the rest also counts as assigned.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that 'unassigned' really means mixed and unclear. Once the חטאת money is removed, the confusion is gone, so the stricter rule no longer applies.

phrases.english: Rava said:
That which we said,
that unassigned money goes to gift offerings,
if the money for the sin-offering fell out from among them,
they are considered as assigned money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הָא דַּאֲמַרַן מָעוֹת סְתוּמִין יִפְּלוּ לִנְדָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining assigned money, רבא limits when money is treated as unassigned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule that unassigned money goes to נדבה applies only while all the money is mixed. Once the חטאת money is separated out, the remaining money counts as assigned.
